pros.title: highly palatable and appealing
pros.explanation: It is an obvious reason people like it.

pros.title: works as a strong flavour booster
pros.explanation: A small amount can carry a whole plate.

pros.title: has strong comfort-food appeal
pros.explanation: It is instantly recognisable and easy to package in meals.

cons.title: sodium is a major drawback
cons.explanation: Even a small serving can bring a lot of salt, so it adds up fast.

cons.title: processing is a major negative
cons.explanation: Because bacon is cured meat, the health tradeoff is bigger than the macro numbers alone suggest.

cons.title: salty, fatty flavour makes portions easy to overdo
cons.explanation: That flavour is part of the appeal, but it also makes bacon harder to keep as a small add-on.

scoreReadiness.summary: Representative finalisation sample with per-100g basis, structured source references, and current scoring/display guardrails applied.
caveats: Real foods vary by cultivar, brand, season, and preparation; this record is a canonical comparison entry rather than a guarantee for every product.

sourceNotes: All displayed nutrition values are stored and checked on a per-100g basis.
Primary and cross-check nutrition references are listed in nutritionDataSources.
Contextual GI and protein-quality fields are optional when not canonical nutrient facts.
Raw bacon FDC 168277 does not expose specific amino-acid rows, so bacon amino_acids_mg uses a labelled cooked-to-raw estimate from cooked pan-fried bacon FDC 168322 scaled by protein ratio.

nutritionDataSources.sourceName: USDA FoodData Central - cooked bacon contrast
MyFoodData Nutrition Data Tools - cooked bacon amino acid mirror

derivation.method: scale cooked bacon amino-acid milligrams by raw protein / cooked-reference protein
